identityDisclosure: Identify Matthias Ramahi as operator and accountable product owner. The public tool may send one short keyword plus optional language and country through a server-side, CAPTCHA- and quota-protected OpenRouter request using one allowlisted OpenAI model. ai-fanout.com stores no raw keyword, final answer, provider response or observed query list. Results are called observed search queries only when the provider response contains the corresponding search-tool action. Never claim access to ChatGPT browser internals, private retrieval traces, system prompts, model reasoning or chain of thought.
standalonePurpose: A free, tightly capped AI Query Fanout Explorer that shows the web-search queries and cited source URLs exposed by an allowlisted OpenAI web-search API run for one short keyword, language and country. If the provider does not return query strings, the tool says so and never substitutes generated guesses.
preferredStrategy: Make the primary product a single-input observed-query utility. A visitor enters one short keyword, optionally selects language and country, completes abuse protection and receives only provider-exposed web-search queries plus cited source URLs, model, provider, timestamp and method version. Use OpenRouter initially with one allowlisted OpenAI model and its server-side web-search tool, hard tool-call and result limits, strict response parsing and a fail-closed unsupported state when query strings are absent. Remove the manual answer-comparison and protocol-builder tools from the public information architecture. Add a bilingual English/German learning hub with a small set of distinct pages about AI query fanout, OpenAI web search, citations, location effects, variability, SEO use and the limits of observation. Keep results useful without signup. Later model comparison is a separate product stage and must preserve provider-specific evidence labels.

forbiddenShortcuts: Calling generated suggestions, citations or source URLs observed search queries when no provider search action exposes those strings
Claiming access to ChatGPT browser internals, hidden Google queries, private retrieval traces, system prompts, chain of thought or model reasoning
Exposing an OpenRouter or other provider key in the browser
Operating without server-side input, output, CAPTCHA, rate, tool-call, daily and monthly budget caps

rightsAndIdentityConstraints: Keyword, language, country and CAPTCHA data may be transmitted only through the documented server-side route after Turnstile and atomic quota reservation; ai-fanout.com stores no raw keyword, final answer, provider response or query list.
Provider-exposed search queries and source URLs are returned ephemerally to the requesting browser and are not published as a retained benchmark or corpus.
Third-party screenshots, copied text, saved model outputs and public examples require verified provenance, attribution, applicable rights and explicit review.
The current stage authorizes an ephemeral single-provider tool, not a retained provider-output dataset, longitudinal benchmark or model-ranking claim.
risks: OpenRouter may count search calls and return citations without preserving every concrete query string in a stable public response field
Observed API searches do not prove what the ChatGPT consumer product would do for the same keyword
Search queries and citations vary by model, provider route, date, language, country and stochastic behavior
Anonymous public web-search inference can exhaust budget or be abused without atomic server-side controls
Returned query lists can encourage low-value scaled pages if treated as a publication plan
